title: Vanishing on compact null sets from an ε + C∫a bound (parent steps 5(i) and 6)
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let (X, ν) be a measure space (ν need not be finite), let q : X → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be measurable and h : X → ℝ ν-integrable. Assume that for every ε > 0 there is C ∈ ℝ such that, for every C^∞ function a : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support and 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, |∫ h(x)·a(q(x)) dν(x)| ≤ ε + C·∫ a dλ, where λ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ. Then ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν = 0 for every compact K ⊆ ℝⁿ with λ(K) = 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (q : X → Euclid n) (h : X → ℝ), Measurable q → Integrable h ν → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → (∀ y, 0 ≤ a y) → (∀ y, a y ≤ 1) → |∫ x, h x * a (q x) ∂ν| ≤ ε + C * ∫ y, a y) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact K → volume K = 0 → ∫ x in q ⁻¹' K, h x ∂ν = 0
